"ASHES OF THE FORGOTTEN

Dark Fantasy Open World RPG

Create a realistic third-person medieval fantasy RPG inspired by The Witcher 3, Elden Ring and Crimson Desert. 

WORLD

Create a small interconnected open world featuring:

- Medieval village, forest and abandoned castle.
- Caves, ruins and hidden treasures.
- Bandit camps and dangerous creatures.
- Dynamic day/night cycle, weather, rain and fog.

PLAYER

Implement:

- Third-person camera and realistic movement.
- Walking, running, sprinting and jumping.
- Sword and shield combat.
- Light/heavy attacks, blocking, parrying and dodging.
- Health, stamina, inventory and equipment.
- Character progression.

COMBAT

Create challenging enemies with different attack patterns and behaviors. Include bandits, mercenaries, undead and monsters. Add one powerful boss with multiple combat phases.

NPC SYSTEM

NPCs must feel alive and independent.

- Give each important NPC a name and personality.
- Implement daily routines: working, eating, sleeping and socializing.
- Add interactive dialogue and merchant systems.
- NPCs should remember player actions and react to reputation.
- Guards patrol, villagers work and flee from danger.
- NPCs should have individual relationships and opinions.

QUESTS AND STORY

Create an original dark fantasy storyline with meaningful choices and consequences. Include main quests, side quests, mysteries and moral dilemmas. Avoid repetitive fetch quests.

GRAPHICS

Use realistic 3D graphics, detailed medieval architecture, cinematic lighting, realistic animations, atmospheric fog and high-quality textures. Avoid cartoon aesthetics.

FIRST PLAYABLE VERSION

Prioritize functionality over map size. Build:

- One village, one forest and one castle.
- 10 named NPCs with daily routines.
- Three enemy types and one boss.
- One main quest and three side quests.
- Functional combat, inventory and equipment.

Make every gameplay system functional. Prioritize immersion, exploration, challenging combat and a believable living world.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable first version of **Ashes of the Forgotten**, a dark-fantasy third-person RPG with an interconnected village, forest, and castle.

## Requirements
- Include movement, combat, health/stamina, inventory/equipment, progression, enemy types, phased boss, and 10 named NPCs with routines, dialogue, trade, opinions, and reactions.
- Include one main quest, three side quests, meaningful choices, and atmospheric day/night, weather, rain, and fog.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Implemented a compact browser-based 3D game using Three.js from a CDN, hand-built low-poly scenery and actors, and custom HTML/CSS HUD and journal.
- Built original story and quest lines around the bell beneath the village and the Bell-Knight.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the world, controls, combat, NPCs, quests, UI, inventory/trading, progression, weather, and endings.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3002 and opened the game in Playwright using Chrome.

### Active
- Fix the game module’s parse error, then validate gameplay and inspect the screenshot.
- Review quest progression and interactions for consistency.

### Blocked
- Browser import of `game.js` fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 't'`; `import('./game.js?debug=1')` confirms it is a syntax error, but its source location is not yet identified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect ternary expressions in `game.js`; several are written without whitespace after `?`, e.g. `heavy?.64:.42`, `boss?.95:1.25`, and `sprint?.62:.35`, which may be parsed as optional chaining.
2. Correct any malformed ternaries, reload `http://localhost:3002`, and confirm no runtime console errors beyond the missing `/favicon.ico`.
3. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/ashes.jpg` and test starting, movement, dialogue, inventory, combat, quest flow, and death/respawn.
4. Fix issues found, then report assumptions and controls to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI structure and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: HUD, menus, dialogue, journal, responsive layout, and title screen.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, actors, NPCs, quests, combat, weather, and game loop.
- `/tmp/opencode/ashes.jpg`: Saved browser screenshot for visual inspection.

## Important Context
- Playwright console reported `Unexpected identifier 't'` at 332ms after page load; the page title loaded but gameplay has not been validated.
- Playwright’s default Chromium executable was missing; using `--browser chrome` opened the page successfully.
- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable first version of **Ashes of the Forgotten**, a dark-fantasy third-person RPG with an interconnected village, forest, and castle.
- Verify gameplay, visuals, interactions, and quest progression; fix issues found.

## Requirements
- Include movement, combat, health/stamina, inventory/equipment, progression, enemy types, a phased boss, and 10 named NPCs with routines, dialogue, trade, opinions, and reactions.
- Include one main quest, three side quests, meaningful choices, and atmospheric day/night, weather, rain, and fog.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based 3D game using Three.js from a CDN, hand-built low-poly scenery and actors, and custom HTML/CSS HUD and journal.
- Developed the original story and quest lines around the bell beneath the village and the Bell-Knight.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`; fixed an earlier parse error caused by the apostrophe in Hobb Fen’s dialogue.
- Added movement input prevention and paused movement/attacks/interactions while appropriate modals are open.
- Reduced renderer pixel ratio and directional shadow-map resolution; disabled shadows on tree foliage and grass.
- Fixed quest pickup visibility updates and increased NPC interaction distance.
- Verified syntax with `node --check game.js` and esbuild; browser checks showed no JavaScript errors.
- Confirmed Maelin’s dialogue and main-quest acceptance work when positioned nearby; quest objective advances to “Follow the bell’s echo into the old crypt.”
- Confirmed W-key movement works: after 24 seconds the player reached z ≈ -20 and the hint showed Maelin in interaction range.

### Active
- Validate complete quest flows, pickups, trade, combat, boss phases/endings, and death/respawn; fix issues found.
- Remove temporary test/debug hooks reintroduced in `game.js`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing from the current `game.js` test hooks; use positions and yaw that put enemies inside attack range before testing damage and boss phases.
2. Test side-quest item pickup and choices, merchant transactions, boss defeat and ending choices, plus death/respawn; fix any issues.
3. Remove `window.__ashesDebug` and `window.__ashesTest` before final validation.
4. Report controls and reasonable assumptions when validation is complete.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, controls, actors, NPCs, quests, combat, weather, game loop, and temporary debug hooks.
- `index.html`: Game UI structure and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: HUD, menus, dialogue, journal, responsive layout, and title screen.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked.
- Maelin is initially near `(0, -11)` and the player starts at `(0, 9)`; direct positioning nearby confirmed dialogue and quest acceptance work.
- The 24-second W-key test did reach Maelin’s range; the objective remained unchanged because interaction was not triggered.
- A recent automated boss test activated the boss at z ≈ -82 but did not defeat it: the player at z = -79 was outside light-attack range. Boss phases and endings remain unverified.
- Temporary `window.__ashesDebug` and `window.__ashesTest` hooks are currently present in `game.js`.

## Ashes of the Forgotten — first version complete

Implemented the browser-based 3D RPG across `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`. The game includes third-person movement, combat and defense, health and stamina, inventory and equipment, progression, three side quests, ten named NPCs, a phased boss, branching choices, and changing weather and time of day.

**Validation passed:** JavaScript syntax and bundling checks; browser startup and quest acceptance; quest-item pickups; merchant transactions; side-quest choices; boss phase transitions and defeat resolution; both ending choices; and death/respawn. The browser test reported no JavaScript errors. I also removed the temporary test hooks and fixed the buried coffer’s repeated mesh creation.

**Validation note:** Boss phase and ending logic were tested in a controlled browser setup; a complete sustained boss fight under normal play was not fully playtested.

**Controls:** WASD to move, mouse to look, F or left-click to attack, R for a heavy attack, Q or right-click to guard, Space to dodge, E to interact, 2 to use a tonic, and I or Esc for the journal.

**Assumption:** The game is delivered as a browser-based experience using Three.js from a CDN, with hand-built low-poly scenery and original quests and dialogue.
